newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat prices stable ahead of new crop trade.
newsitem.headline: German wheat prices stable ahead of new crop trade.

text.p: German wheat prices have stabilised in the old and new crop markets as talks on ex-harvest sales are slowly taking shape, brokers said.
Buying interest was muted and favourable weather reports took the urgency out of negotiations while old crop demand in the domestic market was also subdued.
But brokers reported some sales of high quality old crop to Spain and added the possibility Brussels might resume its weekly grain export tenders this week boosted sentiment.
The Hamburg grain exchange left its spot bread wheat price (12.5 percent protein, 220 hagberg) unchanged from last week's 265 marks a tonne, when it fell by 2.50 marks.
But the spot feed wheat price was cut by 2.50 marks to 260 as the compound feed sector in Germany and the Netherlands reduced its requirements.
Fob Baltic sellers left nominal June delivery wheat at 270-280 marks (12 percent) and material with 13/14 percent protein at 277.50-317.50 marks.
Old crop barley was no longer offered and spot barley in the 3,000 tonne size cost 265 marks fob.
New crop September wheat is now in a 267.50-305 marks range, depending on quality.
New crop rye (July/Aug) indications have been dropped by 10 marks over the last two weeks to 250-255 marks and barley has been set at 237.50-255 marks fob.
